knowledge_point.title: Writing the Flux Across a Closed Surface as a Triple Integral

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=0$, $x=2$, $y=0$, $y=2$, $z=0$, $z=1$. Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(4xz)\,i+(4y^{2})\,j+(1)\,k$, the flux of $F$ across $S$ can be written as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

What is the missing part of the expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4xz)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(4y^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(1) \\  & =4z+8y+0 \\  & =8y+4z.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}(8y+4z)\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,8y+4z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

$$

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}2y^{2}\,\text{d}V,

$$

$$

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS=
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4xy^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3xz)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3y) \\  & =4y^{2}+0+0 \\  & =4y^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}4y^{2}\,\text{d}V,
$$

where $R$ is a type II solid region that can be written as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1,\,y-2z\le x\le -y^{2}-z^{2}+6\}.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}4y^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y-2z}^{-y^{2}-z^{2}+6}\,4y^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Writing the Flux Across a Closed Surface as a Triple Integral

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=0$, $x=1$, $y=0$, $y=2$, $z=0$, $z=1$. Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(x^{2}+y)\,i-(yz)\,j+(4xz)\,k$, the flux of $F$ across $S$ can be written as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

What is the missing part of the expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x^{2}+y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-yz)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(4xz) \\  & =2x+(-z)+4x \\  & =6x-z.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}(6x-z)\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,6x-z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}(22x-4z)\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,22x-4z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-4y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2z^{3}) \\  & =0+(-4)+6z^{2} \\  & =6z^{2}-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}(6z^{2}-4)\,\text{d}V,
$$

where $R$ is a type III solid region that can be written as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1,\,x^{2}\le y\le x-z+5\}.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(6z^{2}-4)\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x^{2}}^{x-z+5}\,6z^{2}-4\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}(xz+6x)\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,xz+6x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}

Let $S$ be the boundary of the finite solid region enclosed by the planes $y=0$, $y=2$, $z=0$, $z=2$, and the surfaces $x=y+z$ and $x=y^{2}+y+z^{2}+z+3$. Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(xy+4z)\,i+(4x+4yz)\,j+(4xz+y)\,k$, the flux of $F$ across $S$ can be written as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS=
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy+4z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(4x+4yz)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(4xz+y) \\  & =y+4z+4x \\  & =4x+y+4z.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}(4x+y+4z)\,\text{d}V,
$$

where $R$ is a type II solid region that can be written as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le 2,\,y+z\le x\le y^{2}+y+z^{2}+z+3\}.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(4x+y+4z)\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y+z}^{y^{2}+y+z^{2}+z+3}\,4x+y+4z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{3}-z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(z)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2xyz) \\  & =0+0+2xy \\  & =2xy.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}2xy\,\text{d}V,
$$

where $R$ is a type III solid region that can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1,\,{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}\le y\le 2}.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2xy\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}^{2}\,2xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=-1,$ $x=0,$ $y=1,$ $y=2,$ $z=0,$ $z=1.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=xy\,i+2y\,j+{x}^{2}zk,$ the flux of $F$ across $S$ can be written as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

What is the missing part of the expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}z) \\  & =y+2+{x}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+y+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+y+2)\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,{x}^{2}+y+2\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-4y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{3}) \\  & =0-4+3{z}^{2} \\  & =3{z}^{2}-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}(3{z}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}V,
$$

where $R$ is a type III solid region that can be written as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x-z+2\}.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(3{z}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x-z+2}\,3{z}^{2}-4\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=-1,$ $x=1,$ $y=0,$ $y=2,$ $z=1,$ $z=2.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F={x}^{2}\,i+xyz\,j+2y\,k,$ the flux of $F$ across $S$ can be written as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\,\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

What is the missing part of the expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2y) \\  & =2x+xz+0 \\  & =2x+xz.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}(2x+xz)\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\,2x+xz\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
